results.claim: THEORY.md, R1. Standard-model data bound with no condition-dependent accuracy loss

human: H-LB-data: Woodworth–Srebro, arXiv:1605.08003v1, Theorem 8, registered iteration conversion
H-LB-zsh: Zhang–Shu–He, arXiv:2010.08766v2, Theorem 3.1 and Section 4.1
H-LB-net: Scaman et al., arXiv:1702.08704v1, Theorems 1–2
comparison.explanation: On the registered class, keeps the data startup term and replaces log(R sqrt(nm/kappa)) by log R, with validity down to a constant R. The improvement is unbounded at the same accuracy inside H-LB-data's range when kappa/(nm) and m/n grow. The proof does not extend the original unrestricted algorithm or component proximal oracle theorem.

coordinates.class: Standard class. The explicit witness has convex, individually L-smooth quadratic components and shared h(x)=mu||x||^2/2. All admissible adaptive randomized algorithms, any fixed message width.
inputs: all standard inputs allowed; no tuning restrictions
coordinates.bound: ceil max { m(1-epsilon/Delta), m log(Delta/epsilon)/(2 log(1/q)) }, q=(sqrt(1+4L/(5nm mu))-1)/(sqrt(1+4L/(5nm mu))+1). In the high-condition regime: ceil(m/4 + sqrt(m L/(n mu)) log(Delta/epsilon)/20).
coordinates.validity: All standard n,m,L,mu,Delta,rho and 0<epsilon<Delta; simple corollary for L/mu >= 5nm and epsilon <= Delta/2.
coordinates.guarantee: Minimax first time to expected gap <= epsilon; one instance obstructs all earlier times seed by seed. Can use W=J.

results.claim: THEORY.md, R2. Smooth local averages alone do not preserve the H-UB order

human: H-UB: Liu–Low, arXiv:2402.02356v1, Theorem 5.1 and Corollary 5.3
H-LB-avg: Zhou–Gu, arXiv:1901.11224v1, Theorem 4.1 (distinct mean-squared assumption)
comparison.explanation: Necessity result: no algorithm can retain the registered H-UB order after replacing individual smoothness by only L-smooth local averages and still tuning the target order with that L. Formal separation includes any fixed powers of logarithms. The two bounds themselves are about different classes.

coordinates.class: PROFILE section 3 local-average smoothness relaxation, with individually theta*L-smooth witnesses for 1<=theta<=m.
inputs: all standard inputs allowed; no restriction on admissible algorithm tuning
coordinates.bound: Same lower expression as R1 with L changed to theta*L inside q. With theta=m the fixed n=2, rho=0, L=m, mu=Delta=1, epsilon=1/m family beats every C m^(5/4) (1+log m)^s bound.
coordinates.validity: 1<=theta<=m, 0<epsilon<Delta; the strict separation has m arbitrarily large on a two-node exact averaging network.
coordinates.guarantee: Uniform hard instance for first-hitting time of every admissible adaptive randomized algorithm; no alternative communication oracle.

results.claim: THEORY.md, R3. Matching two-node bounds by exact averaging and proximal acceleration

human: H-UB: Liu–Low, arXiv:2402.02356v1, Theorem 5.1 and Corollary 5.3
Scaman et al., arXiv:1702.08704v1, Section 3.2 and discussion after Corollary 1
comparison.explanation: Two-node matching bound in the local-average-only relaxation and the standard m=1 case. Exact decoding from a weighted sum removes dependence on the spectral gap and uses one round per accelerated step, but a full local gradient per step can worsen the data count at large m.

coordinates.class: Two-node local-average-only smoothness with differentiable components; all other geometry and oracles unchanged. Positive off-diagonal entry in each row; includes the two-node standard class.
inputs: Delta and epsilon for a certified reporting horizon
coordinates.bound: (m+2) ceil(sqrt(16 L/mu)) ceil_+(log(Delta/epsilon)/log 2); one mixed vector per accelerated step. Matching Theta(m sqrt(L/mu) log(Delta/epsilon)) for R>=2 in the relaxation, and at m=1 in the standard class.
coordinates.validity: n=2, m>=1, L>=mu>0, Delta>0, epsilon>0. No quantitative lower bound on a nonzero off-diagonal weight.
coordinates.guarantee: Deterministic exact proximal algorithm; identical node outputs at the certified time.

results.claim: THEORY.md, R4. Removing connectivity can make the averaged-output problem unsolvable

human: H-UB: Liu–Low, arXiv:2402.02356v1, doubly stochastic matrix assumption and Theorem 5.1
H-LB-net: Scaman et al., arXiv:1702.08704v1, Theorem 2
comparison.explanation: An explicit support-based impossibility for the evaluator's averaged output if the matrix class is weakened to permit the identity. Not a stronger finite-rho network lower bound.

coordinates.class: Standard function and algorithm classes with the communication condition relaxed to rho=1, which admits the identity.
inputs: all standard inputs allowed; no restriction on tuning
coordinates.bound: minimax = infinity when epsilon < Delta (ell/(mu+ell))^2, ell=(n-1)L/(2n).
coordinates.validity: All n>=2, m>=1, L>=mu>0, Delta>0, and 0<epsilon<Delta (ell/(mu+ell))^2.
coordinates.guarantee: A common dimension-two instance misses the target at every time for every admissible algorithm.
